text:
rachel: alerting — p99 for /generate jumped from ~210ms to ~1.9s after the microwindow coalescer tweak at 03:12 UTC. throughput down ~22%. graphs: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/serving/ingest?from=-15m :eyes:

ops-bot: deploy r2026.03.17/patch-317 applied to canary at 03:12:05

liam: saw same. profiler snapshots show a big shift to size==1 batches — ~60% increase in single-request batches. kernel selector now preferring small-token kernel for those shapes.

anika: what's the exact config delta we rolled? snippet from the patch: 
```
batcher.window_ms: 5
batcher.min_coalesce_tokens: 2
batcher.merge_strategy: "aggressive-prefill"
```

devon: KV prefix cache miss-rate spiked at the same time — eviction count +3600 in 10m. looks like prefill ordering + shorter windows are causing churn.

liam: runtime log sample showing kernel decision and exec latency: 
```
[2026-03-17T03:12:14Z] select_kernel(model=opt-13b, batch_shape=(1,20)) -> small-token-kernel
[2026-03-17T03:12:14Z] exec_latency=12ms per-token; call_overhead=1.3ms
```

rachel: notable that p50 is unchanged but p95/p99 exploded. streaming clients are sending many tiny frames which matches the single-batch surge. suspect aggressive coalesce shortened window so many prefill'd requests no longer lined up to trigger the full-kernel path.

anika: hypothesis: decreasing window_ms reduced latency for microbursts but moved the distribution so kernel selector flips to the small-token kernel which bypasses the KV-prefetch fast-path -> more KV misses -> higher tail. plan: revert canary to previous window and collect detailed traces (kernel decisions + kv hits).

devon: rolling rollback to batcher.window_ms=8 on canary now. monitoring panels watching p99, throughput, kv_miss_rate.

ops-bot: rollback complete: r2026.03.17/patch-317 -> r2026.03.16 at 03:18:04

liam: after rollback p99 dropped back to ~230ms and throughput recovered close to baseline. I'll upload flamegraphs + kernel-selection traces to the incident ticket.

rachel: great catch — can you also add a short unit/e2e test that simulates many short streaming prompts? want to catch kernel-affinity flips in CI. tagging @anika for follow-up. :triangular_flag_on_post:

anika: will do. next steps: 1) build repro harness (short streaming prompts + variable window), 2) run grid over {window_ms: 5..12, min_coalesce_tokens:2..4}, 3) instrument kernel-selection to prefer KV-prefill when prefetch alignment likely. propose trying `min_coalesce_tokens: 3` + `window_ms: 6` experiments.

rachel: thanks team — please drop results in #eng-runtime and link the ticket in the weekly perf sync. :thumbsup:
